answer: Randomness-Gated Admission Caps. Each period, an agent gets a per-period admission token by hashing its identity with a verifiable randomness beacon output; only tokens below a threshold admit new sub-agents. The beacon uses a falcon signature so no one can predict outputs ahead of time. A kernel module enforces the cap locally before any sub-agent can act. The delta between expected and actual admitted identities is logged; overruns trigger automatic freeze.
